+def _strip_trailing_zeros(number: str) -> str:
+    """Remove trailing zeros from the fractional part of a formatted number.
+
+    The decimal point goes too when no fractional digits remain, so "3.0" becomes
+    "3" and "2.930" becomes "2.93", while "2.9", "10" and "2.05" are unchanged.
+    Digits before the decimal point and any exponent are never touched.
+    """
+    import re
+
+    # Either keep the digits up to the last non-zero one and drop the zeros after
+    # it (".930" -> ".93"), or drop a fraction made only of zeros (".0" -> "").
+    return re.sub(r"(?<=\d)(?:(\.\d*[1-9])0+|\.0*)(?!\d)", r"\1", number, count=1)
+
+
 def naturalsize(
     value: float | str,
     binary: bool = False,
     gnu: bool = False,
     format: str = "%.1f",
+    strip_trailing_zero: bool = False,
 ) -> str:
